title: Candidate 48's entire known moduli family retains the rank-six half-scalar half-vector obstruction

claim.statement: No sampled point of the exact candidate-48 U(2) x S1 moduli approaches a Lorentz-preserving vector compensator; rank, stabilizer, norm, and scalar/vector split are invariant across the family to numerical precision.
claim.consequence: The MacDowell-Mansouri compensator branch requires leaving the known candidate-48 flat family.

interpretation: The exact-looking invariants strongly suggest that the known finite moduli rotate internal orientation without changing the Lorentz-scalar/vector balance or cross-block singular spectrum.
No local optimization inside this family can produce rank one or a six-generator Lorentz stabilizer if these invariants hold analytically.
The predominantly accidental moduli identified in v647 do not include a hidden compensator direction.
A compensator phase must arise from a different stationary branch, added alignment interactions, or another candidate.
falsifiers: An analytic proof of variation in these invariants, or a counterexample moduli point, would overturn the sampling inference.
The scan covers the established U(2) x S1 parameterization, not undiscovered disconnected moduli.
A compensator built from a different block or composite observable is not excluded.
nextBranches: Derive the exact singular spectrum and one-half projection fractions symbolically from the candidate seed matrices.
Search alternative robust candidate vacua for cross-block rank-one Lorentz-scalar support.
Construct an alignment deformation and follow the bifurcation from the U(1) phase to a Lorentz phase.
